bullets.text: India HRC slipped Rs50/t to Rs63,800/t and rebar fell Rs700/t to Rs63,900/t; the flat-long spread is now -Rs100/t, with long products outpacing flats.
bullets.source: Nomura - India steel - Steel weekly trends (week ended 13 Nov 2026)

detail.summary: Nomura says domestic steel prices stay resilient, with HRC near a four-year high. Rebar has gained momentum faster than HRC, so the flat-long differential has turned negative. Nomura stays positive on the sector and expects the price hikes to more than absorb raw-material inflation in 2HFY27.
points: HRC Rs63,800/t, -Rs50/t w-w
Rebar Rs63,900/t, -Rs700/t w-w
Flat-long spread -Rs100/t
HRC spot margin ~Rs35,640/t in Nov, +Rs2,800/t q-q
Buy on Tata Steel, JSW Steel, Jindal Steel

bullets.text: Imported coking coal is flat w-w at $261/t, about 6% above the 2QFY27 average, while iron ore (62% Fe) is at a CY26 low of $86/t.
bullets.source: Nomura - India steel - Steel weekly trends (week ended 13 Nov 2026)

detail.summary: Global input cost pressure is easing after the coking coal rally, which followed supply disruptions and a fatal mine accident in China. Iron ore is at its lowest level this year.
points: Coking coal $261/t, flat w-w
Coking coal ~6% above 2QFY27 average
China domestic coking coal $330/t, up over 40% since accident
Iron ore 62% Fe CFR China $86/t, CY26 low

bullets.text: India's Oct finished steel imports jumped 66% y-y to 0.76MT while exports fell 32% to 0.44MT, leaving India a net importer by 0.33MT.
bullets.source: Nomura - India steel - Steel weekly trends (week ended 13 Nov 2026)

detail.summary: October data show modest domestic production growth but surging imports against weaker exports. Consumption remains resilient, and India turned a net steel importer for the month.
points: Imports 0.76MT, +66% y-y, +16.4% m-m
Exports 0.44MT, -32% y-y, -22.6% m-m
Net import 0.33MT
Consumption 14.28MT, +6.6% y-y
Crude steel 14.05MT, +0.7% y-y

bullets.text: I-Sec cuts Grasim TP to Rs4,000 from Rs4,175, citing a change in UltraTech's TP; it values UltraTech at a 25% holdco discount.
bullets.source: I-Sec - Grasim Industries (BUY): Soft quarter, yet a promising outlook

detail.summary: I-Sec retains BUY on Grasim but cuts TP to Rs4,000 after a soft Q2FY27 and an 11% FY27E EBITDA cut. The new TP reflects a change in UltraTech's TP, and the holdco discount applied to UltraTech is 25%, justified by continued high dividend income.
points: Grasim TP Rs4,000 vs Rs4,175 earlier
UltraTech holdco discount assumed at 25%
UltraTech dividend to Grasim Rs39.68bn in Q2
Other holdings valued at 40% holdco discount
FY27E EBITDA cut 11%; FY28 risks seen as limited

bullets.text: Kotak cuts NMDC FV to Rs80 from Rs95 and trims FY27/28E EBITDA 4%/8%, as dispatches of 22.2mt lag 1HFY27 output of 27.3mt.
bullets.source: Kotak - [Kotak] NMDC (CMP: Rs70, FV: Rs80, ADD): Dispatch volumes continue to lag output

detail.summary: Kotak keeps ADD but lowers FV to 6x EV/EBITDA from 6.5x because production keeps outrunning sales, building inventory. Receivables from stressed RINL are rising and seaborne ore weakness caps pricing. October shows the same gap between output and dispatch.
points: FV Rs80 vs Rs95; 6x EV/EBITDA Sep-28E
1HFY27 output 27.3mt vs dispatches 22.2mt
2QFY27 EBITDA Rs21.6bn, Rs2,060/t, below estimates
RINL receivables Rs55.6bn vs Rs47.1bn in 1Q
NMDC prices ~16% below import parity

bullets.text: NMDC lump ore price was raised Rs150/t to Rs5,400/t wef Sep-26, with fines steady at Rs4,500/t.
bullets.source: Nomura - India steel - Steel weekly trends (week ended 13 Nov 2026)

detail.summary: Nomura's weekly notes the NMDC lump price hike alongside a weak seaborne ore market. Kotak's NMDC note separately says NMDC cut prices twice in Jul-Aug.
points: Lump +Rs150/t to Rs5,400/t, wef Sep-26
Fines unchanged at Rs4,500/t
Seaborne iron ore 62% Fe at $86/t

bullets.text: Kaynes 2Q miss: revenue +4% yoy, EBITDA margin 13.2%, PAT 47% below consensus, FY26 restated; JPM expects negative reaction, call 16-Nov 8:30.
bullets.source: JPM & Kotak - Kaynes Technology: First Take: Miss led by lower smart meters; restatement of previous year financials

detail.summary: Miss came from lower smart meter sales as management prioritises cutting working capital. A change in auditor led to restated FY26 and 1QFY27 numbers. Kotak flags a 49% stake sale in Kaynes Semicon to Vishay as a call focus.
points: JPM: revenue 8% and EBITDA 17% below consensus
JPM Neutral, TP Rs3,150; consensus cuts expected
FY26 EBITDA restated 9% lower, net income 12% higher
Working capital days 169 vs 163 in 1Q (JPM)
Order book Rs106bn, +31% yoy (Kotak)
Vishay buys 49% of Kaynes Semicon for US$56.4mn (Kotak)

bullets.text: Amber 2Q EBITDA 26% below Kotak on 3.7% margin despite revenue +60% yoy; Kotak FV cut to Rs8,300 from Rs8,600, still BUY.
bullets.source: Kotak - Amber Enterprises (CMP: Rs6,772, FV: Rs8,300, BUY): Growth strong, margins disappoint; focus shifts to ILJIN

detail.summary: Electronics beat strongly but consumer durables margin collapsed on commodity inflation, forex, wages and Sri City ramp-up costs. Focus shifts to the ILJIN electronics IPO, whose DRHP is filed with the OPPO business excluded.
points: Electronics revenue Rs12.5bn, +94% yoy; margin 9.3%
Consumer durables EBITDA margin 0.3%; some pass-through in 3QFY27
Adjusted loss Rs706mn vs Kotak Rs290mn
FY27-29 estimates cut 15.1% to up 1.1%
FY27 guidance kept: RAC-in-line growth, margin down 50-100bps

bullets.text: Avalon raises FY27 revenue growth guidance to ~30% from 26-30%; 2Q revenue +37% yoy, order book +27%; Emkay BUY, TP Rs2,400 unchanged.
bullets.source: Emkay - Avalon Technologies: Strong 2Q results, strong growth prospects ahead; BUY; Target: Rs2,400 (+4 more in Outlook)

detail.summary: Emkay sees the guidance as conservative: about 30% implies only ~20% yoy growth in 2HFY27. It balances strong growth against a share price already up ~132% YTD. TP implies 60x/41x FY28/29E P/E.
points: EBITDA margin 12.6% vs consensus 11.8%
Implied book-to-bill 1.34 vs 1.05 in 1QFY27
Semicon could reach 10% of revenue with one customer
TN government MoU for 25 acres, Rs530-540mn capex
CMP Rs2,050; upside 17.1% to TP

bullets.text: MS sees power shortages emerging 2028 with pricing power shifting to asset owners; stays selective on power equipment, prefers behind-the-meter providers.
bullets.source: Morgan Stanley - IDEA: Energy and Power: Beyond AI: Our Key Ideas

detail.summary: MS argues new gas/coal plants take 4-6 years to build and renewables plus batteries cannot supply dependable power. Power shortages are expected in 2028, and new equipment capacity comes online in 2028-29. Top picks are Asia names (HPCL, Gulf, Keppel), not Indian power utilities.
points: Industry View Attractive; top OW HPCL, Thai Oil, Gulf Development
New power plants take 4-6 years to build
Aircon power demand to match datacenter growth by 2030
Industrial power demand is 2x that of datacenters
Pricing power shifts to asset owners as shortages emerge in 2028

bullets.text: MS estimates ~36trn units of global power use by 2030; consumption outside China is growing 3.3x faster than last decade.
bullets.source: Morgan Stanley - Energy & Power: What's C-Suite Thinking?

detail.summary: MS says power and energy demand has become more inelastic to price, with 2026 consumption surprising to the upside. Rising power prices are speeding grid deployment, and more nuclear and renewables raise the need for behind-the-meter supply. MS hosts C-suite at its Singapore conference over the next five days.
points: ~36trn units of power consumed by 2030, above IEA forecasts
Non-China power consumption growing 3.3x faster than last decade
Europe and Japan power consumption growing after decades of decline
India gas consumption flat despite high LNG prices
Grid deployment need accelerating as power prices rise

bullets.text: I-Sec flags guidance cuts at Infosys, HCLT and Cognizant on soft Q2FY27 growth, and prefers Mphasis, Coforge, Persistent and TechM for near-term visibility.
bullets.source: I-Sec - Technology: IT Services review – Q2FY27: Soft growth in seasonally strong quarter leads to guidance cuts for full-FY27

detail.summary: Q2FY27 sequential growth was softer than expected at most large caps, and TCV is still not converting to revenue. Large-cap EBIT margins are trending down. I-Sec sees no AI revenue offset yet and prefers mid-caps plus TechM.
points: TechM +2.4% QoQ CC, the only large-cap exception
Coforge fresh order intake USD 1bn, up 104% YoY
Large-cap EBIT margin ~100-200bps below pre-Covid average
Coforge H1FY27 EBIT margin 16% vs 13.3% in H1FY26
AI ~10-11% of revenue at TCS and Infosys; growth not offsetting non-AI decline

bullets.source: UBS - Hi Rajvaibhav UBS India: what's trending in India's macro

detail.summary: Food inflation rose to 8.9% from 7.7% on vegetables, pulses and an unfavourable base. CPI is set to stay above the RBI's 6% upper bound for the next couple of months, and UBS sees September-quarter GDP at 7-7.5%.

Food inflation 8.9% vs 7.7%

Real GDP growth seen 7-7.5% in September quarter
India-CEI momentum +2% QoQ; growth to soften in H2 FY27E

bullets.source: GS - [GS Daily] 2027 Macro & Strategy Outlook: raise China-H and India to OW, lower TW and China-A to MW

detail.summary: GS upgrades India to Overweight in both its APAC and EM equity outlooks to balance AI-hardware exposure. It is more hawkish than consensus on the RBI, forecasts CY27 GDP of 7.2%, and recommends long India 30y bonds as oil retreats.

CY27 headline CPI 5.7%, above consensus; core 4.7%
